hindi: स्निग्ध और स्वेदित में, महान् दोष होने पर, मृदु और अल्प औषध वाली बस्ति
english: In (one) who is oiled and sweated, when the doṣa is great, a basti (enema) that is mild and has little drug.
notes: GROUPING: units 42 to 45 read as one statement about a mild basti with little drug: 42 gives the conditions, the verbs are in 43 (haret, janayet), and 44-45 give the signs. The subject basti is carried to 43 and no verb is supplied here. 'snigdhasvinne' is taken as a locative 'in (one) oiled and sweated'; it could also be read as a locative absolute with 'mahādoṣe'. 'mṛdu' and 'alpabheṣaja' are taken as two adjectives of the basti.

words.gram: m. acc. sg., agrees with doṣam

hindi: दोष को उभारकर थोड़ा दोष निकालेगी और प्रवाहिका यानी पेचिश उत्पन्न करेगी।
english: Having stirred up the doṣa, (it) would remove a little doṣa and would produce pravāhikā (dysentery with straining).

text_flags.why: possible: 'utklaiśya' is not a regular form; the gerund of ut-√kliś (causative) is 'utkleśya'; 'ai' is probably a printing slip for 'e' (metre unchanged)

notes: Continues 42 (subject basti, 'it'). Modern equivalent: pravāhikā = dysentery with painful straining at stool (standard). 'alpam' agrees with 'doṣam' (a little doṣa).

hindi: बस्ति और अपान में शोफ यानी सूजन, और जाँघों तथा पिंडलियों में सदन यानी शिथिलता।
english: Swelling (śopha) in the basti (bladder, lower belly) and in the apāna (anus), and sinking (sadana, weakness) in the thighs and shanks.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'janayet' of 43 is carried over and none is supplied. 'basti' here is the organ (bladder, lower belly), not the enema. 'apāna' is taken as the anal region; the other sense, the downward wind (apāna), is possible. Modern equivalents: śopha = swelling, oedema (standard); sadana = sinking, lassitude, weakness (standard).

hindi: जिसकी वायु रुकी हुई है, वह प्राणी बार-बार जोर लगाता है।
english: The being (jantu) whose wind is obstructed strains repeatedly.

text_flags.why: possible: 'bhīkṣṇa' is not a word; the initial a of 'abhīkṣṇam' (repeatedly) seems lost; this fits the sense and gives the 16 syllables of the half-verse

notes: Completes the statement of 42-45. 'pravāhate' is the verb that gives pravāhikā its name: straining, as at stool. 'jantu' is a being, a creature; it is kept literal.

hindi: स्वेदन, अभ्यंग और निरूह, जो शोधनीय यानी शोधन करने वाले और अनुलोमिक यानी अनुलोम गति वाले हों,
english: Sweatings (sveda), anointings (abhyaṅga) and nirūhas (decoction enemas), cleansing (śodhanīya) and ānulomika (following the natural direction) (ones),
notes: GROUPING: 46 and 47 form one statement (verb vidadhyāt in 47), and follow 42-45. The adjectives 'śodhanīyānulomikān' agree with all three accusatives (all masculine); whether they qualify only the nirūhas is not decided. The printed 'śodhanīyānulomikān' may be śodhanīya-ānulomikān (as read) or śodhanīya-anulomikān; ānulomika is kept as in the earlier chunk.

hindi: विधान करे; और लंघन यानी उपवास कराकर उसकी वृत्ति यानी आचरण विरेचन किए हुए के समान रखे।
english: One should prescribe, and, having subjected (him) to laṅghana (lightening, fasting), (prescribe) his regimen (vṛtti) like that of one purged.

text_flags.why: possible: the printed word has no ending for 'vṛtti' as the object of 'vidadhyāt'; 'vṛttiṃ tasya' (his regimen) fits the sense and the 16 syllables; 'vṛttis tasya' (nominative, verb understood) is the other possibility

notes: Completes 46. 'viriktavat' is 'as for one who has been purged'. 'laṅghana' is kept as a term (lightening by fasting). The second 'prescribe' is implied by the accusative 'vṛttim'; the reading rests on the possible correction in text_flags.

hindi: वेग का संरोध यानी रोकना करता हुआ, अथवा अतिमात्रा से पीड़ित,
english: Causing holding back (saṃrodha) of the urge (vega), or pressed by excess quantity,

text_flags.why: possible: the print has a stray tilde (ku~r) and the plural 'kurvanto' does not agree with the singular basti of 49; 'kurvan' is expected, but 'kurvanto' fits the 16 syllables, so this is only suspected

notes: GROUPING: 48-51 form one statement about a basti that is thrown upward; the subject is the basti named in 49 ('bastiḥ'), the verb 'nireti' is in 51. Subject and sense of 'pīḍita' are not stated: 'pressed, squeezed' (the basti pressed by excess quantity) is taken; 'afflicted' (the patient) is the other possibility. 'vegasaṃrodha' is the holding back of a natural urge; which urge is not stated.

words.gram: bahuvrīhi (a- governing all), m. nom. sg.

hindi: अथवा अस्निग्ध, नमक और गर्मी से रहित, अल्प और अल्प औषध वाली बस्ति,
english: Or a basti lacking unctuousness, salt (lavaṇa) and heat, small, with little drug,

text_flags.why: possible: 'agnigdha' is not a word; 'asnigdha' (not unctuous) is the likely word, 's' and 'g' being easily confused in the print

notes: Continues 48. The compound is read with a- governing all three members (without unctuousness, salt and heat), as in the list of 'little oil, salt, drug' defects of chapter unit 6; the alternative is only snigdha negated ('not unctuous, (but) salty and hot'). The reading is not firm.

hindi: अथवा मृदु, वायु द्वारा ऊपर की ओर फेंकी गई, मुख और नासिका से,
english: Or mild, thrown upward by the wind, from the mouth and nose,
notes: Continues 48-49; the verb 'nireti' is in 51, and the subject is the basti of 49.

words.gloss: fainting; nausea; thirst; burning; and others

words.gram: pres. part. pra-√vṛt caus., m. nom. sg.

hindi: बाहर निकलती है, मूर्च्छा, हृल्लास यानी मिचली, प्यास, दाह आदि को उत्पन्न करती हुई।
english: (It) comes out, producing fainting (mūrcchā), nausea (hṛllāsa), thirst, burning (dāha) and the others.

text_flags.why: possible: the extra 'a' in 'tṛḍadāha' breaks the sandhi of tṛṭ + dāha (tṛḍdāha) and makes the half-verse 17 instead of 16 syllables

notes: Completes 48-51. The print writes 'pravarttayan' with doubled t, normalised to 'pravartayan' (recorded once for the chunk). Modern equivalents: mūrcchā = fainting, swoon (standard); hṛllāsa = nausea (standard); dāha = burning sensation (standard).

hindi: उसकी मूर्च्छा के विकार को देखकर शीतल जल से मुख को सींचे।
english: Having seen his disorder (vikāra) of fainting, one should sprinkle the face with cold water.
notes: 'asya' is taken as 'his', going with the fainting and the face.

hindi: आक्लम यानी थकावट के नाश तक पंखा झले और प्राणायाम कराए।
english: One should fan (him) until the destruction of the exhaustion (āklama), and should make (him) do prāṇāyāma (breath control).
notes: 'vyajet' is read as 'should fan' (from vyajana, a fan; probable, the verb is rare). 'āklamanāśāt' is an ablative, here 'up to the destruction of exhaustion'. The person fanned is not named.

hindi: पीठ, पार्श्व और उदर को गर्म हाथों से मसले, मुख नीचे की ओर करके।
english: One should knead the back, sides and belly with hot hands, (him) face downward.
notes: The person is not named. 'adhomukham' is taken as describing the person (face downward); it cannot agree with the neuter 'udaram' in a sensible way. Continues the treatment of the fainting in 52-53.

hindi: बालों में खींचकर हिलाए और व्याल यानी सर्प या हिंसक पशुओं तथा दाढ़ वालों से डराए।
english: Having pulled (him) by the hair, one should shake (him) and frighten (him) with vyāla (snakes or savage beasts) and fanged (ones).
notes: The print writes 'vyāḻa' with ḻ; normalised to 'vyāla' (recorded once for the chunk; the same ḻ appears for l elsewhere in the print). 'vyāla' is a snake or a savage beast; 'daṃṣṭrin' is a fanged or tusked animal; the compound is read as a pair. Continues 52-54 (the person is not named).

hindi: शस्त्रों, उल्का यानी जलती लकड़ी और राजपुरुषों से; क्योंकि इस प्रकार बस्ति नीचे जाती है।
english: With weapons, firebrands (ulkā) and the king's men (rāja-puruṣa); for thus the basti goes downward.
notes: Continues 55 (verb bhīṣayet). 'ulkā' is a firebrand or torch (it also means meteor). 'rāja-puruṣa' is a king's man, an officer or soldier.

hindi: और हाथों तथा वस्त्रों से गले का आपीड़ यानी दबाव करे, मानो वह मर रहा हो।
english: And one should make pressure (āpīḍa) on the throat with the hands and cloths, as if he were dying.
notes: 'mriyate yathā' is taken as 'as if he were dying'; 'in such a way that he dies' is the literal sense and is not intended. Continues 55-56.

hindi: क्योंकि प्राण और उदान के निरोध से, जिसका मार्ग और अधिक भली-भाँति स्थापित हो गया है,
english: For, from the obstruction of prāṇa and udāna, (the one) whose course is the more fully established,
notes: GROUPING: 58 and 59 form one statement: the bahuvrīhi 'suprasiddhatarāyaṇaḥ' (masculine) agrees with 'apānaḥ pavanaḥ' of 59. The sense of 'suprasiddha' ('well established') is literal; the context suggests that the course of apāna, the downward wind, is freed, but this is an interpretation (probable) and is not put in the translation. Sandhi: -tara + ayana gives -tarāyaṇa (ṇ after r).

hindi: अपान वायु उस बस्ति को शीघ्र ही खींच लेती है।
english: The apāna wind (pavana) quickly draws that basti away.
notes: Completes 58. 'apakarṣati' means draws off or draws away; the prefix apa- does not itself say 'down', and 'down' is not added.

words.gloss: kuṣṭha (costus, Saussurea costus; standard); kramuka (areca nut, Areca catechu; probable); paste (kalka)

hindi: और कुष्ठ यानी कूठ तथा क्रमुक यानी सम्भवतः सुपारी का कल्क यानी पिसी लुगदी, अम्ल से युक्त, पिलाए।
english: And one should make (him) drink a paste (kalka) of kuṣṭha (costus) and kramuka (probably areca nut), joined with sour (amla).
notes: Identifications: kuṣṭha here is the drug costus, Saussurea costus (standard), not the skin disease of the same name; kramuka = pūga, areca nut, Areca catechu (probable). 'amla' (sour) is not said to be any particular sour substance; none is added. 'pāyayet' rendered 'should make (him) drink' as fixed in the glossary.

words.gloss: would bring into the natural direction

hindi: उष्णता, तीक्ष्णता और सरत्व के कारण वह भी बस्ति को अनुलोम गति में ले आता है।
english: From heat, sharpness and flowing nature (saratva), that too would bring the basti into the natural direction (anulomayet).
notes: GROUPING: 60 and 61 form one statement; 'saḥ' is the paste (kalka) of 60. 'sara' is the quality 'flowing, mobile'; the word is kept literal. 'anulomayet' is rendered 'would bring into the natural direction', as 'ānulomika' was in the earlier chunk.

words.gloss: trivṛt (turpeth, Operculina turpethum; standard); pathyā (chebulic myrobalan, Terminalia chebula; standard); paste (kalka)

hindi: अथवा गोमूत्र के साथ त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ और पथ्या यानी हरड़ का कल्क, नीचे की ओर अनुलोमन।
english: Or a paste (kalka) of trivṛt (turpeth) and pathyā (chebulic myrobalan) with cow's urine, a downward anulomana (bringing into the natural direction).
notes: Elliptical (a nominal phrase); no verb is supplied. 'pathyā' is taken as the name of the drug (a synonym of haritakī); 'wholesome' is the plain meaning of the word and is not used here.

hindi: पक्वाशय में स्थित होने पर, स्वेदित में, दशमूल का निरूह,
english: When (it) is situated in the pakvāśaya (receptacle of the digested, the large intestine), in the sweated (one), a nirūha (decoction enema) of the daśamūla (the ten roots),
notes: GROUPING: 63 and 64 form one statement (verb vidheyaḥ in 64). 'pakvāśaya' is the lower gut where the digested matter lies (large intestine; standard). The ten roots of the daśamūla are not listed in the text and are not listed here. 'sthite' has no stated subject (the basti or the mishap).

words.gloss: yava (barley, Hordeum vulgare; standard); kola (jujube, Ziziphus jujuba; probable); kulattha (horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum; standard)

hindi: और मूत्र में साधित यव, कोल यानी सम्भवतः बेर और कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी के साथ इसका विधान करना चाहिए।
english: And (it) is to be administered with yava (barley), kola (probably jujube) and kulattha (horse gram) prepared in urine.
notes: Completes 63 (the nirūha is the subject, 'it'). 'mūtra' is urine; which animal is not stated here (cow's urine is named in 62 and 65). 'sādhita' = prepared, as fixed in the glossary.

words.gloss: with; amṛtā (giloy, Tinospora cordifolia; probable); vaṃśa (bamboo, Bambusa arundinacea; probable); shoot (pallava)

hindi: अथवा बस्ति, गोमूत्र में सिद्ध किए हुए, अमृता यानी सम्भवतः गिलोय सहित वंश यानी सम्भवतः बाँस के पल्लवों से,
english: Or a basti with shoots (pallava) of vaṃśa (probably bamboo) together with amṛtā (probably giloy), cooked in cow's urine,
notes: Elliptical: no verb is supplied. 'gaumūtrasiddhaiḥ' agrees with 'pallavaiḥ' (cooked in cow's urine). Identifications: amṛtā = guḍūcī, Tinospora cordifolia (probable; the name amṛtā is also used for other drugs); vaṃśa = bamboo (probable); 'pallava' is a young shoot or leaf-bud.

words.gloss: pūtīkarañja (identity disputed; Caesalpinia bonduc is one proposal)
śaṭhī (identity disputed; Hedychium spicatum and Curcuma zedoaria both proposed)
rohiṣa (a fragrant grass, probably Cymbopogon martinii; probable)

hindi: पूतिकरंज यानी सम्भवतः कंजा, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, उसकी छाल और पत्ते, शठी, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, देवाह्व यानी सम्भवतः देवदारु और रोहिष यानी सम्भवतः रूसा घास से।
english: With the bark and leaf of pūtīkarañja (identity disputed), śaṭhī (identity disputed), devāhva (probably devadāru) and rohiṣa (probably a fragrant grass).

text_flags.why: possible: 'devānva' is not a recognisable word; 'devāhva' (called 'deva', i.e. devadāru) fits the list of drugs and the sense, and 'nva' is easily a misreading of 'hva' in the print

notes: Continues 65 (list of ingredients of the basti). The compound is read as: pūtīkarañja's bark and leaf, then śaṭhī, devāhva, rohiṣa; 'tvak' and 'patra' could instead be separate drugs (bark, leaf) but a bare 'bark' and 'leaf' are not drug names, so the first reading is taken. Identifications: pūtīkarañja is disputed (Caesalpinia bonduc proposed; Holoptelea integrifolia and Pongamia pinnata also named); śaṭhī is disputed (as in the earlier chunk); devāhva = devadāru, Cedrus deodara, only on the possible correction (probable); rohiṣa = a scented grass, Cymbopogon martinii (probable).

words.gloss: with; oil; jaggery; sindhūttha (rock salt; standard)
bilva (wood-apple, Aegle marmelos; standard); and the others; five; roots

hindi: तेल, गुड़ और सिन्धूत्थ यानी सेंधा नमक वाली, विरेचन की औषधों के कल्क से युक्त, बिल्व यानी बेल आदि पाँच मूलों से सिद्ध की गई बस्ति, छाती में स्थित होने पर।
english: A basti with oil, jaggery and sindhūttha (rock salt), having a paste (kalka) of purgative drugs, cooked with the five roots beginning with bilva (wood-apple), when (it) is situated in the chest.
notes: GROUPING: this unit holds 32 syllables in one printed line (two 16-syllable halves: 'satailaguḍa... kalkavān' and 'bilvādi... uraḥsthite'), unlike the neighbouring units of one 16-syllable line. The five roots 'beginning with bilva' are not listed in the text; in the Āyurvedic tradition the group is usually bilva, agnimantha, śyonāka, pāṭalā and gambhārī (standard in the tradition, not stated here). 'taila' is oil, not specified. 'uraḥsthite' is a locative without a stated subject (the mishap or the basti in the chest); the series by seat continues in 68 (head).

hindi: सिर में स्थित होने पर नावन यानी नस्य, धूम; सिर सरसों से ढका जाना चाहिए।
english: When (it) is situated in the head: nāvana (nasal medication), smoke (dhūma); the head is to be covered with sarṣapa (mustard).
notes: Elliptical: no verb is supplied; compare 67 (seat in the chest). 'pracchādyam' is a gerundive, 'to be covered'; the form in which the mustard is used (seeds, paste) is not stated. 'dhūma' is smoke (to be inhaled); kept literal.

hindi: बस्ति अत्यन्त उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, अम्ल या घन, अथवा अत्यन्त स्वेदित के लिए,
english: A basti too hot, sharp, sour or thick, or of one excessively sweated,
notes: GROUPING: 69, 70 and 71 form one statement (verb bhavet in 71): the causes of over-application (atiyoga). 'atisveditasya' is a genitive with no governing noun (basti given to one excessively sweated); the construction is loose. 'ghana' = thick, dense.

hindi: थोड़े दोष में, मृदु कोष्ठ में, अथवा बार-बार प्रयुक्त,
english: In a little doṣa, in a soft koṣṭha (storehouse, belly), or applied again and again,
notes: Continues 69 (the subject is the basti).

hindi: अतियोग की अवस्था को प्राप्त होकर वह कुक्षि के शूल यानी पेट के दर्द का कारण हो सकती है।
english: Having reached the state of over-application (atiyoga), it would become a cause of belly-colic (kukṣiśūla).
notes: Completes 69-70. Modern equivalent: kukṣiśūla = colicky pain in the belly or flank (standard). 'atiyoga' is kept as a term.

hindi: वह, विरेचन के अतियोग के समान आकृति और चिकित्सा वाला।
english: That, similar in features (ākṛti) and treatment (sādhana) to over-application of purgation (virecana).
notes: The instrumental 'virecanātiyogena' is governed by 'tulya' (similar to). The printed 'satulya-' could also be sa-tulya- ('with similar ...'), but 'sa' = 'that' with the instrumental of comparison is the plainer reading. Elliptical: no verb is supplied. 'ākṛti' = features, appearance.

words.gloss: madhūka (mahua, Madhuca longifolia; standard); utpala (blue lotus, Nymphaea species; probable)

hindi: पृश्निपर्णी यानी पिठवन, स्थिरा यानी सम्भवतः शालपर्णी, पद्म यानी सम्भवतः कमल, काश्मर्य यानी गम्भारी, मधूक यानी महुआ और उत्पल यानी सम्भवतः नीलकमल,
english: Pṛśniparṇī (pithvan), sthirā (probably śālaparṇī), padma (probably lotus), kāśmarya (gambhārī), and madhūka (mahua) and utpala (probably blue lotus),

text_flags.why: possible: the other members are accusatives governed by 'piṣṭvā' in 74; the final anusvāra seems to have been lost (the syllable count is unchanged)

notes: GROUPING: an ingredient list continuing in 74 ('piṣṭvā'), 75 and 76 (verbs). Identifications: pṛśniparṇī = Uraria picta (standard); sthirā = śālaparṇī, Desmodium gangeticum (probable; the name sthirā is used for more than one plant); padma = lotus, Nelumbo nucifera (probable; padmaka, a different drug, is not meant); kāśmarya = gambhārī, Gmelina arborea (standard); madhūka = Madhuca longifolia (standard); utpala = blue lotus, Nymphaea (probable).

words.gloss: drākṣā (grape or raisin, Vitis vinifera; standard)

hindi: द्राक्षा यानी अंगूर या मुनक्का और मधूक यानी महुआ को पीसकर, दूध में और चावल के धोवन में,
english: Having ground drākṣā (grape or raisin) and madhūka (mahua), in milk (and) in rice-washing,
notes: Continues 73 (all the accusatives of 73 and 74 go with 'piṣṭvā'; the main verb is in 76). 'kṣīre taṇḍuladhāvane' are two juxtaposed locatives; 'and' versus 'or' is not decided.

hindi: द्राक्षा के, पक्वलोष्ट यानी पके हुए ढेले के, अथवा मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी के प्रसाद यानी निथरे हुए स्वच्छ भाग में,
english: In the clear part (prasāda) of drākṣā, of pakvaloṣṭa (a baked or ripe clod; sense uncertain), or of madhuka (probably liquorice),
notes: Continues 73-74 (liquids for the grinding or mixing). 'pakvaloṣṭa' is kept literal as 'cooked, baked or ripe clod'; the sense is unclear, so nothing is built on it (not enriched). 'madhuka' is read as liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra (probable); the madhūka of 74 (mahua) is a different spelling and may be what is meant here too. 'prasāda' = clearness, the clear settled part.

hindi: डालकर, घी सहित बस्ति को अतियोग से उत्पन्न दाह में प्रयुक्त करे।
english: Having added (it), one should apply the basti with ghee in burning (dāha) arising from over-application (atiyoga).
notes: GROUPING: 73 to 76 form one statement: the drugs of 73-74 are ground (piṣṭvā) in the liquids of 74-75, added (vinīya), and the basti with ghee is applied for the burning of 76. The object of 'vinīya' (the ground drugs) is not stated; 'saghṛtam' is read with 'bastim'. Modern equivalent: dāha = burning sensation (standard).

hindi: स्नेहन और स्वेदन से तैयार किए बिना; भारी, तीक्ष्ण, अतिमात्रा वाला,
english: Without having prepared (him) by oleation (sneha) and sweating (sveda); heavy, sharp, of excessive quantity (one),
notes: GROUPING: 77, 78, 79 and 80 form one statement about a basti applied wrongly; the subject 'bastiḥ' is in 78 and the verb 'karoti' in 80. 'asaṃpādya' is a negative gerund; the person prepared is not named. 'sneha' is oil or oleation; kept as 'oleation (sneha)'.

hindi: बुरी स्थिति में स्थित के लिए, अथवा बुरी तरह लेटे हुए के लिए प्रविष्ट की गई बस्ति,
english: A basti introduced to one badly placed (duḥsthita), or to one lying badly (duḥśayita),

text_flags.suggest: bastirduḥśayitāya (one word with the next token)
text_flags.why: possible: the print splits the compound duḥ-śayitāya by a space; the two tokens are given here as printed

notes: Continues 77. 'duḥsthita' = badly placed or posed (the posture); 'duḥśayita' = lying badly (the manner of lying). The person is not named. The words are split as printed, 'duḥ' being the prefix of 'śayitāya'.

hindi: अविप्रवृत्त होकर वह वायु को कुपित करे; वह विमार्ग में गई हुई,
english: Not properly set going (avipravṛtta), (it) would provoke the wind (marut); that (basti), gone by a wrong path,
notes: The sense of 'avipravṛtta' is uncertain: 'not set going, not moving forth properly' is taken; the combination of a- and vi- is unusual, and 'not issued out' is the other possibility. 'vimārgaga' = gone by a wrong path. The subject is the basti of 78; the verb 'karoti' is in 80.

hindi: अंगों की पीड़ा, जम्हाई, स्तम्भ यानी जकड़न और जोड़ों का भेद यानी फटन करता है।
english: (It) produces pain of the limbs (aṅga-ruj), yawning (jṛmbhā), stiffness (stambha) and splitting (bheda) of the joints.
notes: Completes 77-80 (subject: the basti of 78-79). 'aṅgarujām' is taken as a singular accusative; a genitive plural is the other possibility. Modern equivalents: jṛmbhā = yawning (standard); stambha = stiffness (standard); bheda of the joints = splitting or breaking pain in the joints (kept literal).

words.gloss: saṃstara (a sweating method); and the others

hindi: उसे, जो तेल और नमक से अभ्यक्त यानी लेपित है, संस्तर आदि से स्वेदित,
english: Him, smeared (abhyakta) with oil and salt, sweated with saṃstara and the others,
notes: GROUPING: 81 and 82 continue into the next unit (outside this chunk), which should hold the verb; the object 'tam' is the person of 80. 'saṃstara' is a method of sweating (saṃstara-sveda, a spread bed of heated material; probable); the 'others' (ādi) are not listed. Elliptical: no verb here.

words.gloss: bilva (wood-apple); kola (jujube, probable); yava (barley); eraṇḍa (castor, Ricinus communis; standard); varṣābhū (punarnavā, Boerhavia diffusa; standard); pair of bṛhatī (bṛhatī and kaṇṭakārī, the two prickly nightshades, Solanum species; standard)

hindi: बिल्व यानी बेल, कोल यानी सम्भवतः बेर, यव, एरण्ड यानी अरंडी, वर्षाभू यानी पुनर्नवा और बृहती-द्वय यानी बनभंटा और भटकटैया से।
english: With bilva (wood-apple), kola (probably jujube), yava (barley), eraṇḍa (castor), varṣābhū (punarnavā) and the pair of bṛhatī (the two prickly nightshades).

text_flags.why: possible: 'koḻyava' lacks the a of kola-yava (the half-verse has 15 syllables, 16 with it); 'dvahatī' is read as a misprint of 'bṛhatī' (the pair of bṛhatī is a standard drug pair, and 'dva' is easily a misreading of 'bṛ')

notes: Continues 81 (the verb and the exact use are in the next unit, outside this chunk). The print writes ḻ for l in 'koḻ' (normalised, as in 55). The pair 'bṛhatī-dvaya' is bṛhatī and kaṇṭakārī (standard in the tradition, not named in the text). The two corrections are suggested only; the token is kept as printed.
